text.p: Following are the top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- After protracted anticipation of 13 years since signing of the 1984 Joint Declaration, crown colony of Hong Kong will return to its Chinese motherland.
- Chinese President Jiang Zemin vows to use his historic visit to Hong Kong to reassure international community of China's commitment to territory's future stability and prosperity.

- Convicted rapist Mike Tyson bites champion Evander Holyfield on both ears in third round of scheduled 12-round fight and is disqualified in their World Boxing Association heavyweight title re-match.
- pro-India politician and two others killed when powerful explosion rips through high-security legislators' building in troubled state of Kashmir, police say.

- Eleven days to Singapore's long-delayed national Budget, and business community hopes anxiously for tax incentives to tackle two pressing issues: rising business costs and increasing competition from neighbouring countries.

- Indian government reportedly considering reversal of policies to allow foreign airlines to take stakes in domestic carriers, development that has brought opposition from communists and Hindu nationalists.
- Fretting about flat cellular battery will soon be thing of past when French firm Alcatel introduces world's first mobile phone that can run on standard alkaline batteries.

- Even as Hongkong prepares to become a Special Administrative Region of China, it's been business as usual for Hongkong-Singapore relations, with negotiations underway for Investment Protection and Promotion Agreement.
- Market seers have not done too badly in forecasts for the batch of financial results ended March 31.
- Metro Holdings expects newly opened hotel in Cairns, Australia, Oasis Resort, to be profitable next year.
- After climbing steadily all week, Singapore Telecom shares fell sharply on Friday, tumbling 15 cents to Singapore $2.58, wiping out all price gains made since Monday.
